data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The smallest positive integer is 18, found by treating the congruences as an integer linear program: minimize x subject to x=5a+3, x=7b+4, x\u22651, a,b\u22650.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a smaller non-negative (a,b) solving 5a\u22127b=1 exists, then a smaller x exists.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the constraint a,b\u22650 does not actually bind (i.e., negative a or b could yield a smaller positive x via the lcm wrap), the minimality argument is incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Setting 5a+3=7b+4 gives 5a\u22127b=1. The smallest non-negative solution to this Diophantine equation is (a,b)=(3,2) since 5\u00b73\u22127\u00b72=15\u221214=1. Substituting back: x=5\u00b73+3=18 (equivalently x=7\u00b72+4=18). Because a\u22650 and b\u22650 are required for positive x and the general solution shifts by (a,b)\u2192(a+7t, b+5t), (3,2) yields the minimal positive x.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
